info: LoRa message parsing, threshold checking, alert generation

name: Parse Binary to JSON
Build DB Queries
func:
const payload = msg.payload;
if (!payload || !payload.nodeId) return null;
if (payload.error) return null;

msg.nodeId = payload.nodeId;
msg.sensorData = payload;

msg.query = `SELECT d.id as device_id, d.display_name, d.verbose_chat_id,
  -- Compared in the database on purpose. node-postgres returns a
  -- "timestamp without time zone" as a naive string, which JS then parses in
  -- the process timezone. Postgres runs UTC here and Node runs AEST, so the
  -- value came back ten hours adrift and every watch read as already expired -
  -- which silently disabled the feed rather than merely mislabelling it.
  (d.verbose_until > NOW()) AS verbose_active,
  GREATEST(0, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (d.verbose_until - NOW()))::int) AS verbose_secs_left,
  o.name as owner_name, o.email as owner_email, o.phone as owner_phone, o.notify_via, o.telegram_chat_id, o.pair_code,
  (o.muted_until > NOW()) AS owner_muted,
  json_agg(DISTINCT jsonb_build_object('pin_index', dp.pin_index, 'label', dp.label, 'trigger', dp.trigger, 'alert_level', dp.alert_level)) FILTER (WHERE dp.label != '' AND dp.trigger != 'None') as digital_pins,
  json_agg(DISTINCT jsonb_build_object('pin_index', ap.pin_index, 'label', ap.label, 'low_threshold', ap.low_threshold, 'high_threshold', ap.high_threshold, 'alert_level', ap.alert_level)) FILTER (WHERE ap.label != '' AND ap.alert_level != 'None') as analog_pins,
  json_agg(DISTINCT jsonb_build_object('pin_index', bp.pin_index, 'label', bp.label, 'low_threshold', bp.low_threshold, 'high_threshold', bp.high_threshold, 'alert_level', bp.alert_level)) FILTER (WHERE bp.label != '' AND bp.alert_level != 'None') as bus_pins
  FROM devices d
  LEFT JOIN owners o ON d.owner_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN digital_pins dp ON dp.device_id = d.id
  LEFT JOIN analog_pins ap ON ap.device_id = d.id
  LEFT JOIN bus_pins bp ON bp.device_id = d.id
  WHERE d.node_id = $1
  GROUP BY d.id, d.display_name, d.verbose_until, d.verbose_chat_id,
           o.name, o.email, o.phone, o.notify_via, o.telegram_chat_id, o.pair_code,
           o.muted_until;`;

msg.params = [String(payload.nodeId)];
return msg;

name: Query Device Liveness
query:
SELECT d.id AS device_id,
       d.node_id,
       d.display_name,
       d.last_seen,
       d.stale_after_minutes,
       o.name  AS owner_name,
       o.email AS owner_email,
       o.notify_via,
       (o.muted_until > NOW()) AS owner_muted,
       ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - d.last_seen)) / 60)::int AS silent_minutes,
       (d.last_seen < NOW() - (d.stale_after_minutes || ' minutes')::INTERVAL) AS is_stale
  FROM devices d
  LEFT JOIN owners o ON d.owner_id = o.id
 WHERE d.watchdog_enabled
   AND d.last_seen IS NOT NULL;

label: Telegram Bot
info:
Interactive control surface. Email stays the default channel and needs
nothing of anyone; Telegram is opt-in and adds status on demand, verbose
mode, and (later) questions about history.

Pairing is self-service: every alert email carries a one-tap deep link
bound to that owner. The mailbox is the proof of identity - it is the
address already on file - so no admin issues anything.
